title: Abbasid Caliphate
description: Islamic golden age civilization governed from Baghdad until the Mongol sack of the capital.

title: Achaemenid Persian Empire
description: First Persian Empire founded by Cyrus the Great, spanning the Balkans to the Indus Valley.

title: American Declaration of Independence
description: Thirteen North American colonies declare sovereignty and independence from the British Crown.

title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
description: Dictator perpetuo Julius Caesar murdered by conspiring senators on the Ides of March.

title: Battle of Actium
description: Naval victory by Octavian and Agrippa over Antony and Cleopatra, sealing the fate of the Republic.

title: Battle of Gaugamela
description: Alexander the Great's tactical masterpiece routing Darius III of Persia.

title: Battle of Hastings
description: Norman-French army under William the Conqueror defeats King Harold Godwinson.

title: Battle of Marathon
description: Decisive Athenian victory over the first Persian invasion of Greece.

title: Battle of Salamis
description: Crucial Greek naval triumph crippling Xerxes I's fleet in the Saronic Gulf.

title: Battle of Tours
description: Charles Martel leads Frankish forces to defeat the Umayyad army near Poitiers.

title: Battle of Waterloo
description: Definitive defeat of Napoleon Bonaparte by coalition forces commanded by Wellington and Blucher.

title: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
description: Allied Roman and Visigothic army halts the western offensive of Attila the Hun.

title: Black Death in Europe
description: Bubonic plague pandemic devastating between 30% and 60% of the European population.

title: Byzantine Empire
description: Eastern Roman Empire governed from Constantinople, preserving Roman administrative identity.

title: Carolingian Empire
description: Frankish imperial state revived under Charlemagne following imperial coronation by the Pope.

title: Cartographic Methodology: Tau Projections
description: Proper time coordinate mapping allows localized asynchronous historical evolution on an orthogonal axis.

title: Classical Antiquity
description: Era of classical civilization encompassing Greco-Roman antiquity and the Hellenistic world.

title: Columbus Reaches the Americas
description: Transatlantic expedition sponsored by the Catholic Monarchs initiating global trade integration.

title: Copernicus Publishes Heliocentrism
description: Publication of De revolutionibus orbium coelestium presenting the sun-centered model of the solar system.

title: Coronation of Charlemagne
description: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne Imperator Romanorum at Old St. Peter's Basilica.

title: Coronation of Otto I
description: Papal coronation of King Otto I of Germany as Emperor, founding the Holy Roman Empire.

title: Crisis of the Third Century
description: Near-collapse of the empire under simultaneous civil war, barbarian incursions, and economic hyperinflation.

title: Crucifixion of Jesus of Nazareth
description: Pivotal event in early Christian origins occurring in Roman Judea under Pontius Pilate.

title: Destruction of Carthage
description: Conclusion of the Third Punic War establishing unquestioned Roman hegemony in the western Mediterranean.

title: Destruction of the Second Temple
description: Sack of Jerusalem by Titus ending the First Jewish-Roman War and beginning the diaspora.

title: Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire
description: Emperor Francis II abdicates the imperial crown following Napoleon's victory at Austerlitz.

title: Early Modern Era
description: The era of the Scientific Revolution, global exploration, reformation, and the rise of nation-states.

title: East-West Schism
description: Mutual excommunications formalizing the schism between Latin and Eastern Orthodox Christianity.

title: Edict of Milan
description: Agreement between Constantine I and Licinius legalizing Christian worship in Rome.

title: Fall of Constantinople
description: Ottoman conquest under Sultan Mehmed II closing the Roman imperial succession in the East.

title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: Deposition of Romulus Augustulus by Odoacer closing ancient Western Roman history.

title: First Council of Nicaea
description: Ecumenical council establishing the Nicene Creed and theological consensus.

title: First Moon Landing
description: Apollo 11 lunar module Eagle touches down on the Sea of Tranquility.

title: Founding of Rome
measure-to: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: Mythical foundation of Rome on the Palatine Hill by Romulus and Remus.

title: Great Fire of Rome
description: Urban conflagration devastating 10 of Rome's 14 districts during the reign of Nero.

title: Gutenberg Printing Press
description: Invention of movable type mechanical printing initiating the mass media information age.

title: Hagia Sophia Dedication
description: Justinian I consecrates the imperial cathedral of Holy Wisdom in Constantinople.

title: Historiographical Debate: Periodization of Antiquity
description: Gibbon's catastrophic decline model contrasted with Peter Brown's late antiquity transformation thesis.

title: Holy Roman Empire
description: Central European confederation initiated under Otto I and surviving until dissolution in the Napoleonic Wars.

title: Industrial Revolution
description: Global transition to manufacturing processes, steam power, mechanized textiles, and urbanization.

title: Italian Renaissance
description: Cultural rebirth marked by classical revival, humanism, and revolutionary advances in painting and architecture.

title: Macedonian Empire
description: Kingdom under Philip II and Alexander the Great that toppled Persia and spread Hellenism.

title: Magna Carta Sealed
description: King John of England grants royal charter limiting sovereign power and establishing legal rights.

title: Middle Ages
description: Period in European history extending from the fall of the Western Roman Empire to the fall of Constantinople.

title: Mongol Empire
description: Largest contiguous land empire in world history founded by Genghis Khan.

title: Newton Publishes Principia
description: Isaac Newton formulates universal gravitation and the three laws of classical mechanics.

title: Ottoman Empire
description: Imperial state that succeeded the Byzantines as the preeminent power of southeastern Europe and the Near East.

title: Pax Romana
description: Two-century golden age of Roman stability, judicial harmonization, and monumental civil engineering.

title: Peace of Westphalia
description: Treaties inaugurating the modern system of sovereign nation-states.

title: Principate & Roman Empire
description: Imperial Roman state unified under emperors from Augustus to the death of Theodosius I.

title: Protestant Reformation
description: Martin Luther posts Ninety-Five Theses in Wittenberg disputing the sale of indulgences.

title: Ptolemaic Kingdom
description: Hellenistic dynasty founded by Ptolemy I Soter ruling Egypt until the suicide of Cleopatra VII.

title: Roman Republic
description: Res publica Senatus Populusque Romanus spanning Rome's expansion across the Mediterranean.

title: Sack of Baghdad by Mongols
description: Hulagu Khan's siege and destruction of Baghdad, ending the Abbasid Caliphate.

title: Sack of Constantinople (Fourth Crusade)
description: Western European crusaders divert to storm and plunder the Byzantine capital.

title: Sack of Rome by the Visigoths
influence-to: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: Alaric I's Visigoths sack Rome, the first time in 800 years the city fell to an enemy.

title: Scientific Revolution
description: Epoch of modern scientific emergence from Copernicus's de revolutionibus to Newton's Principia.

title: Seleucid Empire
description: Major Hellenistic state established by Seleucus I Nicator across the Near East.

title: Siege of Jerusalem (First Crusade)
description: Crusaders capture Jerusalem and establish the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

title: Storming of the Bastille
description: Insurrectionary seizure of royal fortress prison sparking the French Revolution.

title: The Enlightenment
description: Intellectual movement celebrating reason, liberty, separation of church and state, and constitutionalism.

title: The Hegira
description: Migration of Prophet Muhammad and followers from Mecca to Medina, marking year 1 of the Islamic calendar.

title: Thirty Years' War
description: Devastating religious and political war across Central Europe ending with the Peace of Westphalia.

title: Treaty of Verdun
description: Partition of the Frankish Empire among the three surviving sons of Louis the Pious.

title: Umayyad Caliphate
description: Second Islamic caliphate headquartered in Damascus, extending from Iberia to the Indus River.

title: Western Roman Empire
description: Administrative Western empire based in Milan and Ravenna until the deposition of Romulus Augustulus.
